bug_semantics: The unauthenticated metatags GET endpoint accepts a caller-controlled URL, checks only that it parses, and then performs a server-side fetch. Because the outbound request does not reject loopback, private, link-local, cloud-metadata, or other reserved destinations and does not safely revalidate redirects, a remote caller can use Dub to reach internal or external services and expose returned metadata or response behavior.
flaw_origin: Commit abe4c8e15ae21bd1db59f709aac874254536bbed first added pages/api/edge/metatags.ts. The new public GET handler read url from the query string, performed only new URL(url).hostname validation, passed it to getMetadataFromUrl, and that helper executed fetch(url). Its immediate parent did not contain the metatags endpoint. Later edits and route relocations preserved this trust-boundary flaw and are rejected as the origin.

The reverse pickaxe begins with abe4c8e15ae21bd1db59f709aac874254536bbed; later a705bab7fb0993c7767e475e84514ad940a92f2c only modifies that file, while `git show --name-status f42b9a957c0bce980dd243fb54ab31e0c6c0b834` reports the later R057 route relocation plus helper add/delete, so neither later edit/move is the BIC. Version evidence: the BIC is an ancestor of the advisory-date snapshot 13f7abc9a6a24c9f83093bf94a48b3bcd8aa02fc, whose metatags helper still calls fetchWithTimeout(url); `git tag` returns no tags. Fix disagreement resolution: the primary set fix_sha and direct_fix_sha to f6e9c6990013f18abdc873d8ce5d2a049d3de014, while the reviewer set both to null because it never landed. The commit is a real one-parent remediation candidate: its parent 9fee29dfd48d8d72d55358dcdd33641c77f19e28 calls fetchWithTimeout(url), and its diff changes that sink to safeFetch(url) and adds HTTP(S), private-address, and redirect protections. But `git branch -a --contains f6e9c6990013f18abdc873d8ce5d2a049d3de014` lists only origin/security-ssrf-safe-fetch; `git merge-base --is-ancestor ... origin/main` exits 1; origin/main is 3462d79674bbe3c1161805d956111c2153fb4c6e and still calls fetchWithTimeout(url). With no landed fix and no patched release boundary, the reviewer wins this disagreement and both fix fields are null; the candidate is evidence of attempted remediation, not a repository fix.
reasoning: The advisory mechanism is the public caller-to-server-fetch trust-boundary failure, so the smallest real BIC is the commit that first created that metatags flow, not a later parser edit, import, rewrite, or route move. Direct comparison with the immediate parent proves the advisory-specific endpoint and vulnerable lines were absent, and the single-parent commit object proves no squash decomposition is needed. AI attribution is restricted to that BIC object, whose signal is absent, therefore the causal verdict is NOT_AI. On the sole disputed field, remediation content alone is insufficient to name a fix: f6e9c6990013f18abdc873d8ce5d2a049d3de014 never entered the default branch or any release, the advisory-date snapshot and current main remain vulnerable, and neither Git tags nor the advisory establish a patched version. This is the explicit unpatched exception, so the closed verdict is gate-complete with null fix_sha and direct_fix_sha.
